name: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO)
summary: A heavyweight Mars orbiter carrying the HiRISE telescope, CTX, CRISM and SHARAD, built to return enormous volumes of data.
outcome: Reached Mars in 2006, aerobraked into a low orbit, and has been operating for well over a decade.
funFact: MRO has sent back more data than all other Mars missions combined.

name: Juno
summary: A spinning, solar-powered Jupiter orbiter that dives beneath the radiation belts every perijove, with its electronics inside a titanium vault.
outcome: Arrived in 2016 after an Earth gravity assist; stayed in a 53-day orbit after an engine-valve issue and went on to an extended mission visiting Ganymede, Europa and Io.
funFact: Juno's three solar arrays span about 20 m and produce ~14 kW at Earth, but only ~500 W at Jupiter.

name: Lunar Prospector
summary: A small, low-cost spin-stabilised orbiter that mapped the Moon's composition, gravity and magnetic fields from a low polar orbit.
outcome: Found evidence of hydrogen concentrated at the lunar poles, consistent with water ice; ended in July 1999.
funFact: Its last act was a deliberate crash into a permanently shadowed crater to look for a puff of water vapour.
